title: A Comparative Study of Prism Adaptation Using Virtual Reality and Conventional Prism Glasses
participants: 40 healthy right-handed adults; within-subject control, prism-lens, VR; counterbalanced; 1-week washout
shift_locus: PL: full-field optical shift with 20-diopter prisms; VR: software-defined deviation, exact rendering locus not clearly specified
shift_schedule_magnitude: fixed 20 diopters approx 11.3 degrees; 96 reaches; no gradual schedule reported
input_and_action_completion: Oculus Touch; right hand; controller button press at believed target location; immediate color feedback sphere
embodiment_visibility: virtual endpoint/hand feedback; arm visibility not clearly specified; trunk/head held forward
tasks_and_assessments: pre/post OLP, landmark, line bisection; repeated reaching exposure
main_findings: VR induced leftward OLP in more participants than prism glasses; OLP aftereffects comparable among dual adapters
terminology_and_gaps: uses clinical PA terms consistently but VR perturbation mechanics are underspecified; fixed test order; no discussion of click-induced measurement disturbance
sandbox_relevance: useful direct VR-vs-physical benchmark; good reason to log perturbation class explicitly

title: Visual but Not Auditory-Verbal Feedback Induces Aftereffects Following Adaptation to Virtual Prisms
participants: 48 healthy right-handers; 4 groups: visual vs auditory-verbal x 0 vs 30 deg
shift_locus: controller/white-rod shift relative to real hand; target remains in stable virtual space
shift_schedule_magnitude: gradual hidden shift to 30 degrees over about 50 to 70 trials, then held to 100 trials
input_and_action_completion: HTC Vive controller in right hand; controller-button press for open-loop and closed-loop endpoints; oral landmark judgments
embodiment_visibility: white rod replaces controller; no arm/body visible; featureless white space
tasks_and_assessments: baseline, adaptation, post-tests; closed-loop and open-loop pointing; line bisection; landmark; randomized/counterbalanced test order
main_findings: visual 30-degree condition produced aftereffects and line-bisection transfer; auditory-verbal feedback did not
terminology_and_gaps: calls effector-shift setup virtual prisms; good example of terminology drift; no Heisenberg discussion
sandbox_relevance: strong reference for feedback-modality variable and gradual hidden shift design

title: Inducing Visuomotor Adaptation Using Virtual Reality Gaming with a Virtual Shift as a Treatment for Unilateral Spatial Neglect
participants: 7 healthy adults; 4 conditions across 2 visits
shift_locus: virtual hand cursor shift on screen; optical-shift comparison with real prisms; non-immersive screen setup
shift_schedule_magnitude: virtual shift set to mimic about 12-degree prism deviation; pre 30, adapt 100, de-adapt 30
input_and_action_completion: Microsoft Kinect plus FAAST; forward reach mapped to mouse click; PED screen task or simple games
embodiment_visibility: hand cursor on screen; skeletal tracking in system but not rich embodiment
tasks_and_assessments: 30/100/30 reach phases; PED or game exposure; fixed order, not randomized
main_findings: VR virtual shift induced measurable leftward aftereffect similar in direction to optical shift
terminology_and_gaps: authors mostly say visuomotor adaptation rather than overstating prism equivalence; very small sample; order effects
sandbox_relevance: not a modern HMD prism protocol, but very relevant for cursor-shift and click-mapped interaction confounds

title: Feasibility Study of Immersive Virtual Prism Adaptation Therapy with Depth-Sensing Camera Using Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy in Healthy Adults
participants: 14 healthy adults
shift_locus: virtual hand trajectory shift only; authors explicitly note it does not shift the full visual field
shift_schedule_magnitude: stepwise by phase: pre, 10 deg, 20 deg, post; 10-pointing blocks and click/rest blocks
input_and_action_completion: Oculus Rift DK2 plus Leap Motion; right index pointing; separate push-button clicking blocks
embodiment_visibility: virtual hand only becomes visible in target-visible area; terminal exposure implemented by software visibility gate
tasks_and_assessments: pointing plus clicking/rest; randomized left/right targets; fNIRS; 60 Hz trajectory logging
main_findings: aftereffect observed; right frontoparietal activation; authors note hand-tracking occlusion errors
terminology_and_gaps: uses VPAT label despite only shifting virtual hand; clear statement of difference from prism goggles
sandbox_relevance: strong source for hand-tracking vs controller tradeoffs and software-defined terminal exposure

title: Long-Lasting Amelioration of Visuospatial Neglect by Prism Adaptation
participants: 7 chronic left-neglect patients in treatment group plus control patients
shift_locus: classical full-field optical shift from wedge prisms
shift_schedule_magnitude: 10-degree rightward optical shift; 20 sessions over 2 weeks
input_and_action_completion: physical pointing with real hand; no button press; terminal exposure through physical setup
embodiment_visibility: real hand only; classical terminal exposure
tasks_and_assessments: logs adaptation effect and aftereffect; evaluates far, near, and personal space neglect; long follow-up
main_findings: long-lasting neglect improvement outlasted short-lived visuo-motor aftereffect
terminology_and_gaps: classical benchmark for adaptation effect vs aftereffect distinction; limited sample size
sandbox_relevance: foundational clinical reference for repeated terminal-exposure PA and transfer beyond sensorimotor bias

title: Adaptation to Virtual Prisms and Its Relevance for Neglect Rehabilitation: A Single-Blind Dose-Response Study with Healthy Participants
participants: 48 healthy adults; 0, 10, 20, 30 degree groups
shift_locus: controller/wooden-rod shift relative to real hand; target stable in VR
shift_schedule_magnitude: gradual hidden shift over about 2 min to 10, 20, or 30 degrees; 100 adaptation trials
input_and_action_completion: HTC Vive controller with trigger-like button; button press in open-loop; red beam for bisection; oral landmark
embodiment_visibility: wooden rod instead of controller; no arm visible
tasks_and_assessments: baseline, adaptation, post, recalibration; open-loop at 4 timepoints; line and space bisection; line and space landmark
main_findings: transfer only in bisection tasks and only in 30-degree group; most participants unaware
terminology_and_gaps: explicitly admits principle differs from wedge prisms; still uses virtual prisms label
sandbox_relevance: excellent benchmark for dose, awareness, bisection transfer, and gradual effector-shift design

title: Sense of Ownership Is Linked to the Speed of Visuomotor Adaptation in Virtual Reality but Not to Generalization, Intermanual Transfer, or Aftereffects
participants: 30 healthy right-handed adults; hand vs cursor groups
shift_locus: 40-degree visuomotor rotation around y-axis; hand or cursor feedback
shift_schedule_magnitude: 144 adaptation trials; explicit and implicit test blocks; washout
input_and_action_completion: Valve Index plus wireless gloves; no endpoint button; dwell-based trial start; no visual feedback in test blocks
embodiment_visibility: virtual hand without arm vs cursor at wrist; real arms fully occluded
tasks_and_assessments: familiarization, baseline, adaptation, refresh, spatial generalization, intermanual transfer, aftereffect, agency ratings
main_findings: hand feedback sped adaptation and increased agency, but aftereffects and transfer were similar
terminology_and_gaps: not a clinical prism paper; uses motor-learning language cleanly
sandbox_relevance: useful comparator for embodiment and non-button endpoint capture

title: From Patient to Musician: A Multi-Sensory Virtual Reality Rehabilitation Tool for Spatial Neglect
participants: 4 USN patients and 4 non-clinical users
shift_locus: no prism shift; multisensory music-based VR rehab
shift_schedule_magnitude: not applicable
input_and_action_completion: HMD plus 2 controllers used as mallets
embodiment_visibility: virtual musical instruments; explicit multimodal feedback
tasks_and_assessments: therapy design paper; subtype background; pilot usability and behavioral observations
main_findings: patients responded across space and corrected head direction toward neglected side
terminology_and_gaps: valuable for subtype taxonomy and personalization argument; not a prism implementation paper
sandbox_relevance: useful for multimodal UI, personalization, and subtype framing, not for prism mechanics

title: An Immersive Virtual Reality Game to Train Spatial Attention Orientation After Stroke: A Feasibility Study
participants: 15 healthy controls and 7 stroke patients
shift_locus: no prism shift; patient-tailored multisensory cueing in neglected field
shift_schedule_magnitude: not applicable
input_and_action_completion: Oculus Rift CV1; right touch controller; explicit button-learning procedure; clinician-operated setup
embodiment_visibility: virtual hand and controller visible; left controller disabled
tasks_and_assessments: rehab game plus computerized cancellation comparison; tailored cue algorithms; multiple pilot phases
main_findings: symptoms were consistent between VR and computerized cancellation; cueing improved target discrimination; feasible and acceptable
terminology_and_gaps: not prism adaptation; supports ecological validity and personalization claims
sandbox_relevance: useful for onboarding, clinician control, target-tailoring, and practical patient deployment

title: Expansion of Body Adaptation Areas for Prism Adaptation Therapy Using Virtual Reality: Head Orientation Experiments on Normal Subjects
participants: healthy normal subjects; exact n not extracted from quick pass
shift_locus: symbolic-body and head-orientation shift; extends PA beyond hand
shift_schedule_magnitude: body-measured target placement; repeated shift and no-shift task sets
input_and_action_completion: inside-out tracked standalone VR; controllers and headset; trigger-based measurement
embodiment_visibility: symbolic body rather than realistic hand or head; target visible area staged
tasks_and_assessments: head-orientation experiments; posture measurement; adaptation beyond hand
main_findings: authors argue PA can be extended to whole-body/head-orientation domain
terminology_and_gaps: terminology extends classical PA substantially; concept drift is part of the contribution
sandbox_relevance: useful if sandbox includes posture/head adaptation or symbolic embodiment modes

title: Development of a Virtual Reality System That Generates Prism Adaptation for Multiple Motor Units
participants: healthy subjects; hand-position and head-position adaptation tasks
shift_locus: symbolic-body shift for hand-position and head-position adaptation
shift_schedule_magnitude: multiple no-shift and shift sets; body-measured target generation; shift/no-shift language
input_and_action_completion: controllers and headset positions measured; trigger press reveals symbolic-body vs target error
embodiment_visibility: symbolic body only; realistic limb not shown
tasks_and_assessments: hand-position adaptation and head-position adaptation; open-loop target visibility staging
main_findings: generated adaptation-like effects for upper trunk and head-position control
terminology_and_gaps: uses PA language but also replaces it with shift/no-shift terminology; very non-standard
sandbox_relevance: frame-setting paper for whole-body taxonomy and explicit disclosure of perturbation class

title: Virtual Reality and Eye-Tracking Assessment and Treatment of Unilateral Spatial Neglect: Systematic Review and Future Prospects
participants: systematic review; no direct participant sample
shift_locus: no single prism implementation; review of VR and ET neglect systems
shift_schedule_magnitude: not applicable
input_and_action_completion: not applicable
embodiment_visibility: not applicable
tasks_and_assessments: review of assessment and treatment studies
main_findings: directly states conventional methods miss milder forms and rarely distinguish subtypes; VR/ET promising for richer process data
terminology_and_gaps: key high-level evidence for subtype and ecological-validity arguments
sandbox_relevance: important background source for claim that subtype-sensitive VR frameworks are still underdeveloped

title: Development and Validation of Virtual Prism Adaptation Therapy
participants: 4 healthy participants
shift_locus: virtual hand rendered at transformed position; real and virtual hand trajectories diverge by software
shift_schedule_magnitude: stepwise phases: non-prism, 10 deg, 20 deg, post; target every 3 s
input_and_action_completion: Oculus Rift DK2 plus Leap Motion; pointing action; endpoint confirmation not clearly specified
embodiment_visibility: virtual hand only; no arm details extracted
tasks_and_assessments: proof-of-concept validation; no rich assessment battery reported
main_findings: rightward errors during prism phases and leftward post-adaptation deviation
terminology_and_gaps: very underspecified on task flow, action completion, and logging
sandbox_relevance: early prototype marker; weak direct design reference unless paired with later Cho paper

title: Exploring Perspectives from Stroke Survivors, Carers and Clinicians on Virtual Reality as a Precursor to Using Telerehabilitation for Spatial Neglect Post-Stroke
participants: 7 stroke survivors, 3 carers, 6 clinicians
shift_locus: no prism shift; telerehab acceptability study
shift_schedule_magnitude: not applicable
input_and_action_completion: trial use of VirtualRehab and C-SIGHT systems; questionnaires and interviews
embodiment_visibility: not the focus; home-use and instruction issues emphasized
tasks_and_assessments: focus groups, interviews, acceptability questionnaires; stroke survivors formally assessed with BIT, line bisection, Broken Hearts
main_findings: overall positive attitude to self-administered VR telerehab; strong emphasis on instructions, hardware, and user ownership
terminology_and_gaps: not a prism paper, but more subtype-sensitive in assessment framing than many PA papers
sandbox_relevance: useful for deployment constraints, instruction design, and home-use considerations

title: ARPA: Augmented Reality Prism Adaptation Induces Sensorimotor and Visuospatial Effects
participants: 48 healthy participants; leftward or rightward ARPA
shift_locus: genuine full-field AR shift: camera feed, real environment, real hand, and virtual target all displaced together
shift_schedule_magnitude: fixed 15-degree leftward or rightward shift; 150 exposure movements; multiple post blocks over about 40 min
input_and_action_completion: Vive Pro plus Leap Motion; physical index-finger pointing to surface; no adaptation button press; landmark via left/right foot pedals
embodiment_visibility: real hand visible through AR; first third of movement hidden by virtual black rectangle
tasks_and_assessments: Pre, Post1-Post9 blocks; real and AR open-loop pointing; landmark; counterbalanced real vs AR order in key blocks
main_findings: robust sensorimotor aftereffects both directions; immediate visuospatial effect only after leftward ARPA; generalization to real environment
terminology_and_gaps: closest AR analogue to classical PA in corpus; excellent action-confirmation design because it avoids right-hand button clicks
sandbox_relevance: top reference for ecological full-field shift, low-Heisenberg interaction, and persistence measurement

title: Simulated Prism Exposure in Immersed Virtual Reality Produces Larger Prismatic After-Effects Than Standard Prism Exposure in Healthy Subjects
participants: 20 healthy participants; within-subject randomized condition order
shift_locus: full-field VR implementations via frustum rotation or frustum skew; compared with physical prism goggles plus PC
shift_schedule_magnitude: fixed 10-degree VR conditions; PCP originally 8.7 degrees transformed to 10; 5-step protocol with reset
input_and_action_completion: HTC Vive controller; menu button used to define fingertip; physical PCP touchscreen with beep; reset task included
embodiment_visibility: virtual fingertip only; virtual black box hides arm; haptic rumble on virtual wall touch
tasks_and_assessments: pre-test, baseline, exposure, post-test, reset; randomized condition sequence and 10-min breaks
main_findings: both VR conditions produced larger aftereffects than physical prism condition; rotate and skew similar
terminology_and_gaps: strongest paper on rendering-level implementation differences; button press and fatigue noted but not treated as measurement confound
sandbox_relevance: critical source for perturbation-class comparison and explicit reset procedure

title: Mechanisms Underlying Neglect Recovery After Prism Adaptation
participants: 16 chronic neglect patients plus 8 control patients
shift_locus: classical full-field optical shift with 10-degree prisms
shift_schedule_magnitude: 10 daily sessions over 2 weeks; pre 60, exposure 90, post 30 trials
input_and_action_completion: physical pointing with right index from sternum; no button; terminal exposure through wooden box
embodiment_visibility: real hand; visible and invisible pointing conditions
tasks_and_assessments: BIT plus eye-movement reading task; error reduction and aftereffect tracked
main_findings: error reduction in first week predicted neglect recovery better than aftereffect; oculomotor leftward deviation linked to recovery
terminology_and_gaps: careful distinction between error reduction and aftereffect; excellent mechanistic terminology anchor
sandbox_relevance: important for logging and reporting variables beyond simple aftereffect magnitude

title: Neglect Rehabilitation by Prism Adaptation: Different Procedures Have Different Impacts
participants: 30 neglect patients pseudo-randomized to TPA, CPA, NP
shift_locus: classical full-field optical shift with 10-degree prisms; comparison of terminal vs concurrent exposure
shift_schedule_magnitude: fixed 10 daily sessions; 90 pointing movements per session
input_and_action_completion: physical pointing to pen; no button; terminal or concurrent visibility determined by box setup
embodiment_visibility: real hand; TPA exposes only final part, CPA about half of movement
tasks_and_assessments: BIT pre/post; eye movements in prism groups
main_findings: all groups improved, but terminal exposure outperformed concurrent exposure and neutral pointing
terminology_and_gaps: explicitly shows procedure-level visibility schedule changes the treatment effect
sandbox_relevance: very important justification for making exposure visibility a first-class sandbox variable

title: Combined Virtual Reality and Haptic Robotics Induce Space and Movement Invariant Sensorimotor Adaptation
participants: 60 healthy participants across active, sham, near/far, and robot-guided conditions
shift_locus: rotation between real hand and virtual hand in VR with haptic robot; PA-like rather than literal prism shift
shift_schedule_magnitude: gradual visuo-motor rotation during training; active and robot-guided variants
input_and_action_completion: robotic arm support plus trigger button; active reach or guided movement; haptic feedback
embodiment_visibility: virtual hand with haptic interaction; embodiment/agency/ownership questionnaire
tasks_and_assessments: open-loop reaching, reaching straight ahead, landmark, awareness/embodiment measures
main_findings: aftereffects seen across spaces and even in guided condition; guided condition reduced awareness
terminology_and_gaps: authors speak of VR-PA while using rotation logic; good comparator for active vs passive exposure
sandbox_relevance: useful for guidance mode, haptics, and awareness variables

title: Virtual Reality-Based Sensorimotor Adaptation Shapes Subsequent Spontaneous and Naturalistic Stimulus-Driven Brain Activity
participants: 45 healthy participants in rightward, leftward, or sham groups
shift_locus: VRPA-like adaptation training; details largely inherited from earlier VRPA setup
shift_schedule_magnitude: fixed leftward or rightward adaptation then fMRI pre/post
input_and_action_completion: VR training plus aftereffect tasks; exact interaction hardware not central in this paper
embodiment_visibility: VRPA setup with behavioral aftereffect tasks before/after neuroimaging
tasks_and_assessments: resting-state and naturalistic-video fMRI around VR adaptation training
main_findings: adaptation altered large-scale connectivity and naturalistic responses; POS upregulation correlated with aftereffect
terminology_and_gaps: strong evidence that VRPA changes more than endpoint error, but not a granular implementation paper
sandbox_relevance: secondary support for broader consequences of adaptation; low value for endpoint mechanics

title: Sensorimotor Adaptation in Virtual Reality: Do Instructions and Body Representation Influence Aftereffects?
participants: 30 healthy adults; control, misinformation, arrow groups
shift_locus: whole virtual environment displaced 11.31 degrees to the right; hand vs arrow representation
shift_schedule_magnitude: familiarization 30, baseline 10, exposure 35, de-exposure 30; fixed 20-diopter equivalent
input_and_action_completion: Valve HMD plus HTC Vive hand tracker; no endpoint button; acoustic cues; chinrest
embodiment_visibility: virtual hand or 3D arrow; tracker on right hand; correspondence reinforced on table edge
tasks_and_assessments: baseline, exposure, de-exposure; magnitude from first no-feedback trial; persistence over remaining 29 trials
main_findings: misinformation reduced persistence; body representation had no clear effect
terminology_and_gaps: uses sensorimotor-adaptation language and explicit error-attribution framing; cleaner than many VRPA papers
sandbox_relevance: excellent source for instruction effects, non-button interaction, and embodiment manipulation
